flags.name: California
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of California, known as the Bear Flag, is the official flag of the U.S. state of California. The precursor of the flag was first flown during the 1846 Bear Flag Revolt and was also known as the Bear Flag.

credit.artist: Original: Donald Graeme Kelley Vectorization: Devin Cook

flags.name: Texas
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Texas, also known as the Lone Star Flag, is the official flag of the U.S. state of Texas. Along with the flag of Hawaii, it is one of two state flags to have previously served as a national flag of an independent country.

flags.name: Florida
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Florida is the official flag of the U.S. state of Florida. The flag consists of a red saltire on a white background, with the state seal superimposed on the center. The current state flag was adopted on November 6, 1900, and has only been changed once on May 21, 1985 when the state seal was standardized.

flags.name: New York
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The coat of arms of the U.S. state of New York was formally adopted in 1778, and appears as a component of the state's flag and seal.

flags.name: Pennsylvania
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Pennsylvania consists of a blue field on which the state coat of arms is displayed.

flags.name: Illinois
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The great seal of the state of Illinois is the official emblem of the U.S. state of Illinois, and signifies the official nature of a document produced by the state. The present seal was designed and proposed in 1868 and officially adopted in 1869.

flags.name: Ohio
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Ohio, also known as the Ohio Burgee, is a red, white, and blue U.S. state flag with a distinctive triangular swallowtail shape. The flag's elements symbolize the state's natural features and order of admission into the Union.

flags.name: Georgia
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Georgia bears three horizontal stripes and features a blue canton containing a ring of 13 white stars that encircle the state's gold-colored coat of arms, with the motto of the United States, "In God We Trust", below. Its current iteration was adopted on February 19, 2003.

flags.name: North Carolina
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the state of North Carolina, often referred to as the North Carolina flag, N.C. flag, or North Star, is the state flag of the U.S. state of North Carolina.

flags.name: Michigan
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Michigan is a coat of arms set on a dark blue field, as set forth by Michigan state law. As of 2025 Michigan has had three state flags, and the current flag was adopted on August 1, 1911. The governor has a variant of the flag with a white field instead of blue one.

flags.name: New Jersey
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The coat of arms of New Jersey was adopted in 1777 and modified in 1928. It depicts a shield with three plows flanked by two women. Above the shield is a horse's head atop a knight's helmet. Below everything is a banner that reads Liberty and Prosperity 1776.

credit.artist: author of xrmap, with modifications by Denelson83 and ChrisRuvolo

flags.name: Virginia
flags.about: State of the United States of America

credit.artist: LadyofHats with additional editing by 痛 and Patrickneil / Charles Keck

flags.name: Washington
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Washington consists of the state's seal, a portrait of George Washington, on a dark green field with optional gold fringe. It is the only U.S. state flag with a green field, as well as the only state flag with the likeness of a U.S. president.

flags.name: Arizona
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Arizona is the official flag of the U.S. state of Arizona. It consists of 13 rays of red and gold on the top half. The center star signifies copper production; Arizona is rich in copper, producing more copper than other states in the country.

flags.name: Massachusetts
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts was adopted on March 18, 1908, and has only been changed once in 1971 with the removal of the reverse side. The flag features the coat of arms of the Commonwealth on a white field.

flags.name: Tennessee
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Tennessee is the official flag of the U.S. state of Tennessee. The flag displays an emblem on a field of red, with a strip of blue bordered by white on the fly. The emblem in the middle consists of three white stars on a blue circle also with a white border.

flags.name: Indiana
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Indiana was adopted on May 31, 1917, as the third official flag of the U.S. state of Indiana. Designed by Paul Hadley, it has remained unchanged since its adoption, with specifications standardized in 1955. Prior to 1955, it was referred to as the state's official banner.

credit.artist: The Indiana state flag was designed by Paul Hadley in 1917. This SVG file was made by Zsco

flags.name: Maryland
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Maryland is the official flag of the U.S. state of Maryland and the 17th-century heraldic banner of arms of Cecil, 2nd Baron Baltimore. It consists of the arms of his father George, 1st Baron Baltimore (1579–1632), quartered with those of his grandmother, heiress of the Crossland family.

flags.name: Missouri
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Missouri was adopted on March 22, 1913, when governor Elliot Woolfolk Major signed the State flag act making it official. Its design consists of a triband of three equal horizontal stripes colored red, white, and blue, with the state coat of arms in the center.

flags.name: Wisconsin
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Wisconsin was first adopted in 1863, and was modified in 1979. It is a blue flag charged with the state coat of arms of Wisconsin.

flags.name: Colorado
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Colorado was officially adopted on June 5, 1911. The flag, designed by Andrew Carlisle Carson, consists of a fess design of three horizontal stripes of equal width, with the top and bottom stripes colored blue, and the middle stripe colored white.

credit.artist: Original: Andrew Carlyle Carson Vector: Fleminra

flags.name: Minnesota
flags.about: State of the United States of America

credit.artist: Original: Minnesota State Emblems Redesign Commission Vector: Jamie Eilat , Undertiago

flags.name: South Carolina
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of South Carolina is a symbol of the U.S. state of South Carolina consisting of a blue field with a white palmetto tree and a white crescent. Roots of this design have existed in some form since 1775, being based on one of the first American Revolutionary War flags.

credit.artist: Design by South Carolina General Assembly , SVG by Steve Hall

flags.name: Alabama
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Alabama was adopted by Act 383 of the Alabama Legislature on February 16, 1895, following the introduction of the bill by its designer, Representative John W. A. Sanford Jr. Its design features a crimson cross of St. Andrew on a field of white. A St.

flags.name: Louisiana
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Louisiana consists of a rectangular field of blue with the arms of Louisiana, a pelican vulning herself, in white in the center, with a ribbon beneath, also in white, containing in blue the state motto: "Union Justice Confidence".

flags.name: Kentucky
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, a U.S. state, was adopted by the Kentucky General Assembly on March 26, 1918. It features a navy blue field with the Commonwealth's seal at its center, the words "Commonwealth of Kentucky" above, and sprigs of goldenrod, the state flower, below.

flags.name: Oregon
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Oregon is a two-sided flag in navy blue and gold with an optional gold fringe. On the front is the escutcheon from the state seal, and on the reverse is a gold figure of a beaver, the state animal. Oregon is the only U.S. state to feature different designs on either side of its flag.

flags.name: Oklahoma
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Oklahoma, also known as the Oklahoma flag, is a rectangular field of sky blue on which is placed an Osage war shield with six crosses and seven pendant eagle feathers above the name of the state in a white Eurostile text in all capitals.

flags.name: Connecticut
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Connecticut is a white baroque shield with three grapevines, each bearing three bunches of purple grapes on a field of royal blue. The banner below the shield reads "Qui Transtulit Sustinet," Latin for "He who transplanted sustains," Connecticut's state motto.

credit.artist: Jean-Pierre Demailly, xrmap authors, Commons users (SVG)

flags.name: Utah
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: he flag of the U.S. state of Utah was adopted on March 9, 2024, and is one of the official flags of the state. It is a horizontal tricolor of irregular blue, white, and red bands, with the white band featuring a gold-outlined blue hexagon containing a gold beehive above a five-pointed white star.

flags.name: Iowa
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Iowa is a vertical tricolor flag designed by Dixie Cornell Gebhardt in 1917. Iowa legislators officially adopted the flag in 1921.

flags.name: Nevada
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Nevada was adopted in 1929, when governor Fred B. Balzar signed into law a bill adopting the new flag. Its design consists of a solid cobalt blue field with, in the upper hoist quarter, two crossed sprays of sagebrush forming a half-wreath.

flags.name: Arkansas
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The state flag of the U.S. state of Arkansas, also known as the Arkansas flag, is a red banner charged with a large blue-bordered white lozenge (diamond). Twenty-nine five-pointed stars appear on the flag: twenty-five small white stars within the blue border, and four larger blue stars in the white diamond.

flags.name: Mississippi
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Mississippi is the official flag of the U.S. state of Mississippi. Its design consists of a white magnolia blossom surrounded by 21 stars and the words "In God We Trust" written below, on a blue Canadian pale with two vertical gold borders on a red field.

credit.artist: Rocky Vaughn, Sue Anna Joe, Dominique Pugh, Clay Moss, Kara Giles, Micah Whitson and the M

flags.name: Kansas
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Kansas represents the U.S. state of Kansas. Designed by Hazel Avery in 1925 and adopted in 1927 after Kansas Adjutant General Milton R. McLean pushed the legislation that adopted the flag, its design features the Kansas state seal and a sunflower on a blue field.

flags.name: New Mexico
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of New Mexico, also referred to as the New Mexican flag and Zia Banner, is a state flag, consisting of a sacred red sun symbol of the Zia tribe on a field of gold (yellow).

flags.name: Nebraska
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Nebraska, was adopted in 1925. It features a blue field with the Nebraskan state seal at its center, rendered in gold and silver colors. The flag was adopted following the introduction of a bill by Representative J. Lloyd McMaster in the former Nebraska House of Representatives.

flags.name: Idaho
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The seal of the U.S. Territory of Idaho was adopted in 1863 and redrawn several times before statehood in 1890. The first state Great Seal was designed in the 1890s by Emma Edwards Green, the only woman to design a U.S. state seal. That seal was used until 1957, when the seal was slightly redrawn by Paul B.

credit.artist: Paul B. Evans, based on a work by the Adjutant General of Idaho and Emma Edwards Green

flags.name: West Virginia
flags.about: State of the United States of America

flags.name: Hawaii
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Hawaii, also known as the Hawaiian flag, is the official flag of the U.S. state of Hawaii. Along with the flag of Texas, it is one of two state flags to have previously served as a national flag of an independent country.

flags.name: New Hampshire
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The seal of New Hampshire, codified by law in 1931, features the frigate USS Raleigh, encircled by a laurel wreath and nine stars. A granite boulder appears in the foreground, while water represents the harbor of Portsmouth. The U.S.

flags.name: Maine
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Maine was adopted by the U.S. state on February 23, 1909. Its design consists of the state's coat of arms on a blue field. In the center of a heraldic shield, a moose rests under a tall pine tree. A farmer and seaman are meant to represent the traditional reliance on agriculture and the sea by the state.

flags.name: Rhode Island
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The state flag of Rhode Island is the official flag of the U.S. state of Rhode Island, consisting of a white background and a gold anchor in the center surrounded by thirteen gold stars, for the original Thirteen Colonies and Rhode Island's status as the 13th state to ratify the Constitution.

flags.name: Montana
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Montana consists of the state's name above the state seal centered on a blue field. The flag was adopted in 1905, largely resembling a flag made by Harry Kessler in 1895.

flags.name: Delaware
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of Delaware consists of a buff-colored rhombus on a field of colonial blue, with the coat of arms of the state of Delaware inside the rhombus. Below the rhombus, the date December 7, 1787, declares the day on which Delaware became the first state to ratify the United States Constitution.

flags.name: South Dakota
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The current flag of South Dakota was adopted in 1992 to represent the U.S. state of South Dakota.

flags.name: North Dakota
flags.about: State of the United States of America

flags.name: Alaska
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Alaska displays eight gold stars, forming the Big Dipper and Polaris, on a dark blue field. The Big Dipper is an asterism in the constellation Ursa Major, which symbolizes a bear, indigenous to Alaska.

flags.name: Vermont
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Vermont displays the state's coat of arms and motto on a rectangular blue background. The Vermont General Assembly adopted the flag on June 1, 1923.

flags.name: Wyoming
flags.about: State of the United States of America
flags.story: The flag of the U.S. state of Wyoming was adopted on January 31, 1917. Its design consists of a blue field bordered by white and red, with a white silhouette of an American bison in the center, bearing the state seal rendered in blue on its side.
